mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous two months indicates a strengthening economy, which boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with positive housing starts, or the correlation between housing starts and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous month signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE changes and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% annually, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy in a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% annually and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous month, it signals strong consumer demand and a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS annual growth > 5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.5pp in 1 month
regime_hint: strong consumer demand with labor market tightening
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS growth and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 over the previous month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS changes and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is below its 12-month moving average, it indicates accommodative monetary policy with low inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with low inflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
